prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations (monitoring alerts only); Adverse Weather Mode (Duty Manager may reduce remote stands); Capacity Reduction State (tighter escalation); both allow binding metering, revised rates; Recovery Phase (remote stands absorb late arrivals); Contingency Fallback State (Contingency Operations Console). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; fix saturation vs Airport Capacity Plan -> Tactical Regulation Proposal); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; uses crew/rotation constraints to offer/retain/exchange/release CTT); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; receives only feasibility result, timing boundary); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter (Runway Lighting Outage Card); East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove); Collaborative Decision Log (reasons, constraint, actor, approval time, outcome, crew-legality/preference constraint); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; SHALL NOT advance aircraft unless remote stand release supports taxi plan); Gate Conflict Detector; Airline Interface Adapter (crew legality indicators, no personal data); Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet latency; notifies Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; MUST refresh apron within 5 s); Common Situation Display (measures; crew states feasible/time critical/infeasible/operator review required, no commercial reasoning); Audit Event Ledger (recovery choice: who, effective time, flight, reason category); Business Rules Registry (preference fields mandatory/optional/hidden); Identity Access Service (enforces visibility for Portal, Digital Briefing Room, APIs); Sector Load Monitor (Departure Fix Load Sheet -> Regional Flow Manager); Flight Data Exchange (distributes only approved result); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Data Governance Steward; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard). En-route constraint records validated by Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison confirms conditional capacity. Crew legality

Document units:
S639: Performance Analytics Warehouse may analyze anonymized patterns of legality constraints and recovery selections to improve disruption playbooks.
S640: The design allows coordinated recovery during Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase while preserving the operator's commercially sensitive decision logic.
S641: Apron cleanliness and stand readiness checks are treated as operational prerequisites before any surface movement release is accepted into the departure sequence.
S642: The Ramp Control Lead defines the sweep areas by stand, taxilane, service road interface, and equipment staging zone so that each check has a clear spatial boundary.
S643: Ground Handling Dispatcher assigns qualified personnel to perform apron sweeps during planned turnaround milestones and after any event that may introduce foreign object debris.
S644: Foreign object debris checks cover paved stand surfaces, jet bridge wheel paths, towbar storage locations, belt loader positions, fueling lanes, and adjacent drainage grates.
S645: East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting surveillance cues, but visual confirmation remains required where sensor coverage is obstructed by parked aircraft or ground equipment.
S646: The Ramp Movement Board displays stand readiness status using time-stamped states that distinguish unchecked, under inspection, cleaned, blocked, and ready conditions.
S647: Ramp Control Lead sends the Apron Sweep Completion Note after the responsible sweep team confirms that the assigned apron area is clean, safe, and free of observed foreign object debris.
S648: Airport CDM Portal uses the shuttle count to confirm that remote-stand passenger transfer demand is consistent with stand readiness timing.
S649: The Airport CDM Portal records each stand readiness confirmation with the stand identifier, responsible organization, inspection time, readiness constraint, and confirming user identity.
S650: Identity Access Service restricts readiness confirmation privileges to approved ramp, handling, and airport operations roles to prevent unverified operational releases.
S651: Time Synchronization Service provides the common time reference for sweep records, readiness confirmations, and safety-related release decisions.
S652: When a sweep identifies debris, leaking fluid, damaged pavement, unsecured equipment, wildlife activity, or lighting damage, the stand remains unavailable until the hazard is removed or mitigated.
S653: Ground Handling Dispatcher updates the Handling Resource Planner when personnel, equipment, or cleaning vehicles are reassigned to restore a contaminated stand.
S654: The Ramp Control Lead reviews unresolved hazards against active turnaround demand before allowing pushback planning to continue for the affected stand.
